newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Body of S.Africa activist killed by police exhumed.
newsitem.headline: Body of S.Africa activist killed by police exhumed.

text.p: South Africa's "truth commission" on Friday exhumed the body of a fourth political activist murdered in the 1980s by apartheid security police in KwaZulu-Natal province, investigators said.

The Umdloti grave site was pointed out to Nobel laureate Desmond Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission by six former security policemen who have applied for amnesty for killing 10 anti-apartheid activists in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

Investigators working with the commission, which is probing crimes committed by both sides of the apartheid divide, earlier this week uncovered three other burial sites after they were identified by the policemen.
The sites, on the north coast of the Indian Ocean Province, are on farms leased under false names by the security police.

The fourth body was found face down in a metre-deep grave in a vegetable garden behind a house set in a lush sugar cane plantation about 30 km (20 miles) north of the Indian Ocean port city of Durban, commissioner Richard Lyster said.

"We have found the body of an activist who was allegedly murdered by the police who are claiming amnesty for the act," Lyster told reporters after a six hour search with a mechanical digger, a team of five men with shovels and two sniffer dogs.
The body had been covered in lime to speed up decomposition and there were two small neat holes on each side of the skull which was missing its front teeth.

"The person was obviously shot in the side of the head. From the look of the remains the person had their hands tied behind their back but we are unsure at this stage if the body is in the kneeling position," said a policeman at the scene.
The identity of the victim was withheld until the family was notified.
Commission spokesman Mdu Lembede said the three bodies uncovered earlier in the week had been found in a crouched positions with bullet holes in the top of their skulls.
"It looked as though the victims were made to sit in holes dug in the ground and then shot in the top of the head execution style," Lembede told Reuters.
One of the activists, Portia Ndwandwe, had been kidnapped in Swaziland and taken to the farm to be interrogated and "turned around" by security police to work for them, Lembede said.
Earlier this week Lembede said the six policemen had confessed to throwing two other bodies into a river after shooting their victims.
"The applicants also confirmed that four more people were blown up in such a way that very little remained of their bodies," he said.
The commission, which has until the end of this year to look into 30 years of human rights abuses, has the power to grant perpetrators amnesty if they confess in full to their crimes.
